$doc: DEEP-LINK VECTORS — one table, three test suites (Phase 13.4, #278/#282).
The deep-link ROUTE TABLE is already generated (RouteGen). What was not was the
URL -> route PARSE, hand-written twice: MainActivity.parseDeepLinkRoute in Kotlin
and BnDeepLink.route(from:) in Swift. They disagreed on multi-segment routes —
Android returned host only and dropped the path — and nothing compared them.
You cannot generate a parser from a manifest. You CAN generate the table it must
satisfy. tools/BlazorNative.WireGen emits a test table per language from this
file; a case is written ONCE and all three suites assert it.
route: null means the URL must produce NO route (rejected, not coerced).
TO ADD A CASE: add it here, run `dotnet run --project tools/BlazorNative.WireGen`,
and commit the regenerated files. Never hand-edit a .g.* file.

vectors.why: the common case — both shells already agree
THE DIVERGENCE (#278): Android returned /settings and dropped /audio
trailing slash trimmed — two spellings of one route would be a silent table miss
empty authority, explicit path — Android reads data.host (null here), iOS reads url.host (empty); the two APIs disagree about where the first segment lives
wrong scheme is REJECTED, never coerced into a route
